subject: Security attestation refresh + log-hold and throughput amendment for renewal
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@orionpay.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@orionpay.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: SOC2 re-attestation + retention horizon and throughput questions

Hi Marcus / Karthik,

As we prepare to renew our contract (term ends 2027-07-31) we need to confirm a couple of items the security and procurement teams flagged:

1) Retention / log-hold: Our compliance team wants audit logs retained in a searchable export for 365 days (currently set to 90 days in the contract). Can Redwood provide an updated path for a 365d retention window and an export cadence for our auditors? If there are format constraints please note them.

2) Temporary throughput for evidence ingestion: During the attestation window (target week of 2027-07-10) we expect to ingest and export large log batches — approximately 15 TB of compressed logs. We need to understand dedicated capacity or burst options, SLA impacts, and the cost for a one-week uplift.

3) Evidence packaging: TUV (our auditor) requires a sample export (2 weeks) in their preferred schema and a list of events included. Can you confirm you can deliver a sample by 2027-06-18?

I've attached our SOC2 question set and a sample request. Procurement is looped for any contract amendment / addendum.

Next steps we need from Redwood: timeline to enable 365d retention toggle, sample export delivery date, and an estimate for the uplift cost.

Thanks,
Sarah
Security Ops Lead, OrionPay
Attachments: orion-soc2-questions-2027.pdf, sample-log-export-2027-05.tar.gz
From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@orionpay.com>, TUV-Audit Ltd <audit@tuv-audit.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, procurement@orionpay.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC2 re-attestation + retention horizon and throughput questions

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Laura and Vanessa for the technical and commercial details.

Immediate answers:
- Retention toggle: We can enable a 365-day archived retention window. There are two modes: 1) cold archive (cost-optimized, slower exports) or 2) warm-archive (queryable export within 24h). We recommend warm-archive for audit timelines.
- Sample export: We can deliver a 2-week sample in TUV's schema format by 2027-06-17 if we get a confirmation on which fields are required (see TUV note below).
- Throughput uplift: For a 15 TB compressed export during the attestation week we recommend a Dedicated burst reservation for the 7-day window to avoid queuing; I'll include an estimate in the next message.

Proposed immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
1) TUV confirms schema fields by 2027-06-09.
2) Redwood prepares and delivers sample export by 2027-06-17.
3) Procurement signs amendment for 365d retention and a 7-day burst (DocuSign link provided once we finalize cost).

Laura / Vanessa: Can you (a) validate the export schema compatibility, (b) provide the warm-archive cost delta and approximate burst pricing for a 15 TB export, and (c) confirm any change to our SLA during the burst window?

Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
From: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC2 re-attestation + retention horizon and throughput questions

Thanks Marcus — quick technical notes after looking at the attachments and a sample log dump: 

- Schema compatibility: The sample log format Sarah sent maps cleanly to our event model; TUV's required fields (timestamp, request_id, model_id, user_id_hash, routing_decision, kv-cache-ops) are present. We will need a lightweight transformation for two fields (user_id -> user_id_hash, and expanded routing metadata). That transformation can be part of the export pipeline.
- Warm-archive option: Indexed, queryable exports for 365d will add ~0.25 USD per GB-month on top of standard retention. For 15 TB compressed (~45 TB expanded) that's an estimated incremental cost of $2,750 for the month bucket covering the audit export window.
- Burst capacity for export: To guarantee no queuing during the week, recommend reserving 8x export slots for 7 days. Estimated one-week reserved burst cost: $4,100 (includes I/O throughput and temporary compute reservations).
- SLA: No change to core latency SLOs for production traffic — export bursts isolate the export pipeline and we will throttle background jobs to preserve production capacity. We'll provide a one-week runbook for export start/stop.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf (contains our export template and transformation notes).

I'll prepare a short pricing addendum for procurement to review.

—Laura
Director, Trust Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: TUV-Audit Ltd <audit@tuv-audit.com>
To: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com, Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@orionpay.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC2 re-attestation + retention horizon and throughput questions

Hi Marcus / Sarah,

Quick clarifying questions from the audit team:
1) For user identifiers: can you confirm whether you will deliver user_id_hash using SHA256 salted with a per-customer salt, and whether salts are reversible within Redwood? Auditor preference is non-reversible hash with customer-provided salt.
2) For time windows: we need contiguous event coverage for the sample (2027-05-23 to 2027-06-05). Will the transformation pipeline preserve original timestamps and timezone info?
3) Chain of custody: please include an MD5/SHA256 manifest for each export bundle and record the export job id and initiating user.

If you can confirm those points we can sign off on the sample format and proceed with the attestation checklist.

Regards,
Julia Meier
Lead Auditor, TUV-Audit Ltd
From: marcus_lin@redwood.example.com
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@orionpay.com>, TUV-Audit Ltd <audit@tuv-audit.com>, procurement@orionpay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.example.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 16:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: SOC2 re-attestation + retention horizon and throughput questions

Hi all — confirming items and next steps below (finalizing M.A.P.):

1) Hashing & salts: We will apply SHA256 with a customer-provided salt for the user_id_hash; Redwood will not retain a reversible mapping. We will accept a salt via secure upload (we will provide a KMS-wrapped key exchange).
2) Timestamps: Original timestamps and timezone offsets will be preserved in the export. The transformation pipeline will not alter event timestamps.
3) Chain of custody: Each export bundle will include a SHA256 manifest and metadata (export_job_id, initiated_by, start/end timestamps).

Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- By 2027-06-09: TUV confirms final schema field list (Julia).
- By 2027-06-17: Redwood delivers the 2-week sample export (2027-05-23 -> 2027-06-05) in TUV schema.
- By 2027-06-18: Redwood provides pricing addendum and DocuSign amendment for 365-day warm-archive retention + 7-day burst reserve.
- Target week 2027-07-10: Execute the export and evidence handoff.

Procurement / Legal: Once you confirm, I'll send the DocuSign amendment for the retention change and the one-week burst reservation (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/sign/abc123-amendment).

If there are no objections I'll proceed to produce the sample on 2027-06-15 and share the export manifest.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf
